finding: tests/test_signal_search.py:331 Stale-projection tests never exercise the required rebuild path.
rationale: The locked contract requires a rebuildable projection and the selected AC6 design makes an explicit second build the stale-recovery path, but the stale-input matrix builds only once, checks rejection and unchanged projection bytes, and never proves that an existing stale projection can be replaced or queried with changed canonical content; the current os.replace implementation does not supply regression coverage for that observable contract.

evidence.output: AC1 requires a rebuildable projection, and AC6 requires binding input hashes and rejecting or rebuilding stale projections.
The plan explicitly states: “Rebuilding is an explicit call to build_signal_projection; a read never silently rebuilds,” and AC6 says “an explicit build is the rebuild path.”

Each stale-input case calls build_signal_projection once, mutates one canonical input, asserts search_signals raises StaleSignalProjectionError, and asserts the projection digest is unchanged; there is no second build or post-rebuild query.
All successful build calls are initial builds in separate tests; no test calls build_signal_projection twice on the same case root.

The current builder allows existing owned artifacts and replaces staged projection and manifest files with os.replace, so the implementation presently supports replacement, but no test would fail if that replacement behavior regressed or were changed to reject an existing stale projection.
